The *Pubbaṅgamiyattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 292) is a canonical Pali verse text preserved within the Therāpadāna collection of the Khuddaka Nikāya [SuttaCentral]. It relates the biographical narrative and karmic background (apadāna) of the elder (thera) Pubbaṅgamiya. SuttaCentral records five modern translations in five languages [SuttaCentral].
No direct external parallels in Chinese, Sanskrit, or Tibetan corpora are listed by SuttaCentral, and DharmaNexus identifies no cross-language matches meeting its threshold [DharmaNexus]. Within the Pali tradition, however, DharmaNexus detects widespread formulaic text reuse, comprising 56 matching passages shared across 19 other texts [DharmaNexus]. The most substantial sharing occurs with the *Theragāthā-aṭṭhakathā* (17 matches, 1,081 characters; notably segments 5.1–6.2) [DharmaNexus]. Recurring Apadāna verses—particularly across segments 5–10—are also widely shared with other Therāpadāna poems, including the *Pupphacchattiyattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 331), *Sattapāṭaliyattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 257), *Adhopupphiyattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 86), and *Ekañjaliyattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 352) [DharmaNexus].
